comparisons.peer_topic: Data Center Segment Product Portfolio and Strategy
comparisons.peer_summary: The Data Center segment includes server-class CPUs, GPUs, AI accelerators, DPUs, FPGAs, SmartNICs, and Adaptive SoC products. The company leverages these technologies to address computational, visual data processing, and AI workload acceleration needs by enabling optimization of performance and power for diverse workloads.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and AMD describe a broad, multi-architecture portfolio strategy to address diverse computing workloads beyond traditional CPUs. Intel explicitly labels its approach as 'xPU,' encompassing CPUs, GPUs, IPUs, FPGAs, and accelerators, stating that different workloads benefit from different architectures. AMD mirrors this with its Data Center segment description, listing server-class CPUs, GPUs, AI accelerators, DPUs, FPGAs, and SmartNICs, and noting that different combinations of these products enable optimization for a diverse set of workloads.

sentences.text: Beyond the CPU, we deliver a family of xPU products encompassing client and data center GPUs, IPUs, FPGAs, and other accelerators.
The xPU approach recognizes that different workloads benefit from different computing architectures, and our broad portfolio helps meet our customers' increasingly diverse computing needs.
The Data Center segment primarily includes server-class CPUs, GPUs, AI accelerators, DPUs, FPGAs, SmartNICs, and Adaptive SoC products.
Different combinations of CPUs, GPUs, DPUs, FPGAs, SmartNICs, and Adaptive SoCs enable the optimization of performance and power for a diverse set of workloads.
